extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, naturalists, educators, and scholarly correspondents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for judging scientific books, taxonomic/observational contributions, letters to the editor, and field/practical methods (as used in 19th-century scientific periodicals). Emphasises fairness in controversy, pedagogical design, accurate citation, and clear observational reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair quotation and contextual accuracy in controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid quoting only the part that suits you and omitting immediately following passages that change the meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer criticises Prof. Zollner for quoting selectively: 'Prof. Zollner here quotes the part that suits him, leaving out altogether the portion (immediately following) which turns the charge entirely the other way.' Standard: when attacking another author’s argument, reproduce context faithfully and avoid truncation that misrepresents the opponent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensational or ad hominem imputations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make sensational imputations of discourtesy or worse, especially against venerable philosophers, without clear evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece objects to 'the sensational imputation of discourtesy, if not of something worse' and to nationalistic invective ('Deutschland iiber Alles, and down with every Deutscher who sees aught to admire or to respect beyond the limits of Germany !'). Standard: maintain civility, avoid nationalistic or personal denunciation in scholarly dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and concision in elementary textbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: A good elementary arithmetic text proceeds gradually but is never tedious, with copious explanation yet no superfluous verbiage; 'Every page is to the point.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As applied to Temple A. Orme’s book: smooth transitions between rules, clear exposition without unnecessary words, and material suited to the young minds for which it is intended. Evaluate pages for directness and absence of padding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical pedagogy and use of concrete materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer methods that combine palpable (manipulative) with written arithmetic; use of blocks or substitutes is strongly recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit recommendation from the Preface: 'Teachers are strongly recommended to take every available opportunity of using suitable blocks of wood to represent units, tens, hundreds, and thousands... without these blocks ... the subject will become too abstract.' Criterion for elementary math texts: include/manufacture practical, manipulable aids and instructions for their classroom use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach reasoning over rote rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage pupils to rely on reason and to develop their own processes rather than merely memorising rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted aim: pupils 'will frequently make out processes of their own for arriving at truths, having been taught to rely not on rules, but on reason.' Textbooks and teachers should scaffold discovery and logical understanding, and include examples/exercises that permit pupil-constructed methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptable and appropriately sized exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a good store of simple and varied exercises which may readily be curtailed or enlarged according to individual cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical editorial note: exercises should be flexible for different abilities; look for exercises of varying length and difficulty and explicit guidance on adaptation for students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical accuracy in pedagogical works
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimise typographical faults; correctable errors should be few and insignificant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer notes typographical faults on pp. 30, 104, and 105. Criterion: check for typesetting errors that could mislead learners; count and classify errors when assessing a teaching book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and dissemination of translations/publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate and publish important foreign contributions as separate, affordably priced editions so interested readers in other countries can obtain them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer: it 'would have been an advantage had this “Contribution” made its appearance in the trade as a separate publication with a London publisher, at a fixed price.' Criterion for editors/publishers: ensure translations are widely and affordably available rather than hidden in obscure journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for taxonomic / mycological contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions should include a good digest of existing literature, personal observations (e.g., mycelium and spore growth), synopses relating parasites to hosts, and detailed measurements and descriptions of germination and promycelia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the review of Fischer von Waldheim: 'The memoir now published commences with a very good digest of the literature... personal observations on the mycelium and spore growth... The synopsis of the Ustilaginez in relation to their supporting plants and the place of their spore formation will be very useful... The details of the germination of spores, direction and character of the promycelia, the effects of moisture, light, &c., measurements of threads and spores, all combine to render this a useful contribution.' Use these elements as checklists when evaluating taxonomic papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial policy for letters to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor disclaims responsibility for correspondents’ opinions and will not consider anonymous communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated policy: '[T]he Editor does not hold himself responsible for opinions expressed by his correspondents. No notice is taken of anonymous communications.' Submissions should be signed and responsible; editorial offices should state and enforce anonymity policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for observational / meteorological reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of earthquakes or storms should state dates, locations, times, barometer readings, wind directions and strengths, and observed effects (damage, shipwrecks), and note limits of communication/observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (typhoon at Cebu): the correspondent provides timed barometer readings, wind directions and strength, sequence of events, and observed consequences ('About eighteen vessels were thrown on shore... many houses unroofed...'). Criterion: include quantitative instrument readings when available and precise temporal/location data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate citation and faithful representation in scientific disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: When disputing another scientist’s claim, check the original publication and cite exact passages or experimental details to avoid misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the water-analysis exchange: the writer points to the original 1867 paper to show the contested statement about nitrogen recovery. Standard: verify quotations and experimental descriptions in the primary source (include page numbers) before asserting that an author’s claim is 'untrue.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision of definitions and logical consistency in scientific argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Define key terms (e.g., 'energy', 'work', 'potential') clearly; avoid conflating distinct concepts and ensure internal logical consistency when making theoretical claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the debate on conservation of energy: criticisms hinge on vague or inconsistent uses of terms ('Mr. Brooke says that “energy is the power of doing work.” He does not tell us what he means by work.'). Criterion for reviewers/letter-writers: demand precise definitions and consistent use of foundational terms, and avoid basing conclusions on premises that are neither provable nor disprovable without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field collection technique for butterflies (practical method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach a settled butterfly with slow, regular motions from a short distance and pick it up with the fingers; fold wings if necessary to avoid damaging the specimen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice from an entomologist: 'All your motions when near the butterfly must be slow and regular... When the wings are in this position the butterfly is caught with least damage to its plumage. ... If the butterfly does rise take care not to change your slow and steady motions.' This is a valid alternative to nets when appropriate, trading speed for preservation of specimens.
